limitations: The reference covers the current setuptools find declarations and explicit Hatch wheel-package declarations. Setuptools py-modules/explicit package lists and Hatch force-include, remapping, custom hooks or alternate inclusion routes fail with a reviewed-adapter requirement; generated modules, binary-only extensions and unknown backends likewise need real adapters.
This proves declared source placement, tracked presence and flat-name collision absence; it does not build artifacts or prove installed import origin or behavior.
Migration must update build metadata, relevant direct source-path references and isolated artifact tests while preserving public import/CLI names.
This does not prescribe a common monorepo component topology or require every repository to become a workspace.

Native C sources and separately owned NOTICE/formal resources have evidenced reasons to remain outside Python src. The reference reports their source-expansion routes as adapter-required; it does not label their existence unnecessary drift or claim their builds qualified.
